chapter: Building the band: Dave Duncan, Denver and Rene Hall
title: The Tulsa Club hires a Black band for the first time
summary: A head waiter pushes Fields' seven-piece band into the exclusive Tulsa Club for a week, including the Skelly daughter's party, a first for Tulsa.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: So this being Grant Williams' home, he decided he's going to stay, and so he joined my band and so the captain at the Tulsa Club--

Bruce Steele was in there, a terrific white band, and when he was leaving and they would pay a band on a week stand. So they had an opening and this head waiter, Johnson--Captain Johnson--the manager said why don't you see how you feel, give them a try, and so this manager of the hotel, he said well, I don't know whether they'll go for it. He said try it anyway. He even told him let him audition, see what you think about him. He said, well you know about it than I do, if you said all right, I'm just wondering how they'll think about it and everything.
Then he told him about this white trombone player, he said I'll give a week in there.
But you couldn't have a mixed band?
Yeah, couldn't have a mixed band.
How big a band did you have now?
I had about seven pieces then; that's all.
So we went on in this Tulsa Club and he came with us a lot and be around but before we left, you know, he sat in--
This was at the Tulsa Club? Now I'm confused.
This was not at the Louvre Ballroom?
No, this was the Tulsa Club. Very exclusive.

And so later on, I didn't know really how much it counted, but they had two firsts--I think about five years later, like they have what happened on this date in such and such a town--and they had it in there, they weren't saying black then, it was colored or negro, for the first time the Tulsa Club used a negro band for a week and the negro band played the Joanne Skelly outgoing party.

oil millionaire that had come in to Tulsa, the Skelly Oil Company, and so we played his daughter's coming out party. That was all in the news what happened. And like suddenly everybody got history, well not long ago, senior citizen showed me a book that somebody in Tulsa had written, that one of the newspapers put out, and showed the Tulsa of yesterday, and they had it in there about Ernie Fields, the first negro, and they had all the pictures in there, the first negro band that played the Tulsa Club.
